1. Scope — Dimensional and other requirements for double-ended uterine curette, Sim's pattern 

with both ends sharp.

FIG. I CURETTE, UTERINE, DOUBLE-ENDED, SHARP, SIM'S PATTERN 



3. Material — Stainless steel conforming to Designation 22Cr13 or 30Cr13 of Schedule V of 
IS : 1570-1961 ' Schedules for wrought steels for general engineering purpose '. 

4* Workmanship and Finish 

4.1 The suffaces of the curette shall be free from pits, dents, burrs, scales and other defects. 

4.2 All the edges shall be even. The edges shall be rounded except the working ends, which shall be 
semi-sharp. 

4.3 The curette shall be passivated and polished bright. 

5. Heat Treatment — The instrument shall be hardened and tempered to 400 to 450 HV measured as 
near to the working ends as possible.

6- Tests 

6*1 Clamp the curette in a vice at the middle of the handle to its long axis- Suspend a load of 
30 N (3 kgf approximately) gradually on one working end at a distance of 15 mm from the 
tip. Similarly carry out the test on the other working end. On completion of the test the curette shall 
show no sign of damage. 

6.2 Scrape with one working end of the curette a piece of 6-mm hard millboard quickly and 
vigorously to and fro 20 times with moderate degree of force. Similarly carry out the test with 
the other working end. The surface of the millboard shall be scraped easily and cleanly with both the 
ends, and on completion of the test the curette shall not show any sign of damage or distortion. 

6.3 Corrosion Resistance Test — Scrub the curette with soap and warm water, rinse in hot water and 
then dip in 95 percent ethyl alcohol. Dry the curette, immerse in copper sulphate solution at room 
temperature for 6 minutes and wash with fresh water or wet cotton wool. 

The copper sulphate solution shall be made up as follows: 

Copper sulphate (CuS0 4 .5H 2 0) 40 g 

Sulphuric acid ( HUSCh ) (spgrV84) 100g 

Distilled water [see IS: 1070-1960 Specification 900ml 

for water, distilled quality ( revised) ] 

There shall be no red stains or spots on the curette after the test, but dulling of the polished 
surface may be permitted. 

7. Marking — The curette shall be marked with the following: 

a) Manufacturer's name, initials or recognized trade-mark; and 

b) The words ' Stainless Steel \ 

7.1 tSf Certification Marking — Details available from the Indian Standards Institution. 

8. Packing — The curettes shall be wrapped in moisture-proof paper or packed in polyethylene bags. 
avoiding contact with one another. 



Reprography Unit, ISI, New Delhi, India
